library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jeon_2025_efineptakin_alfa"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jeon_2025_efineptakin_alfa"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70252> (open access; Supporting
  Information Text S1 is the final NONMEM control stream and Table S1 the
  provenance of the fixed parameters)
* Primary trial report (demographics and NCA used below): Lee SW et al.
  Clin Transl Sci 2020;13:1161-1169, <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12800>

Efineptakin alfa (rhIL-7-hyFc; development codes GX-I7 and NT-I7) is a
homodimer of two recombinant human IL-7 molecules fused to a hybrid
IgD/IgG4 Fc ("hyFc"), 104 kDa. The Fc lets it bind the neonatal Fc
receptor (FcRn) and escape lysosomal catabolism. Jeon et al. (2025) fitted
a semi-mechanistic model to the microdose phase 1 trial in healthy adults
and used it to propose IM dosing regimens for lymphopenia.

The model has three states:

* `abs_site` -- the injection-site / interstitial space that receives the SC
  or IM dose. It exchanges with central in both directions (`Q / V_I` out,
  `Q / V_C` on free drug back) and feeds the endosome at `k_uptake`. The
  apparent volume `V_I` is route-specific (`ROUTE_SC`).
* `central` -- serum. Drug binds IL-7R (CD127) at quasi-steady state
  (QSS-TMDD, `R_tot = 1360 pmol/L`); the complex is internalised at `k_int`
  and free drug is cleared at `CL`.
* `endosome` -- a lumped FcRn-recycling endosomal space (apparent volume
  `V_D`). Drug binds FcRn (92 uM) at quasi-steady state; the complex leaves
  at `k_recycle`, 71.5 % to central and the rest back to the injection
  site.

All amounts are pmol of IL-7: the drug is dosed in pmol of rhIL-7-hyFc and
`f(abs_site) = 2` counts its two IL-7 moieties. The observation `Cc` is the
**free** IL-7 concentration in serum (pmol/L), which the authors assumed the
baseline-adjusted ELISA measured.

# Population

The model was fitted to 410 baseline-adjusted serum IL-7 concentrations
from 24 healthy adults in the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
phase 1 trial NCT02860715 (Seoul National University Hospital). Thirty
subjects were randomized 8:2 to drug or placebo in three single-dose
cohorts: 20 ug/kg SC, 60 ug/kg SC and 60 ug/kg IM (8 active subjects per
cohort). Jeon 2025 does not tabulate demographics; the trial report (Lee
2020) gives mean +/- SD age 27.1 +/- 6.0 years, height 1.70 +/- 0.08 m,
weight 65.3 +/- 11.1 kg and BMI 22.4 +/- 2.4 kg/m^2, with men and women
19-45 years eligible. Stepwise covariate modelling of age, sex, weight,
height and BMI retained no covariate, which the authors attribute to
weight-based dosing.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Jeon_2025_efineptakin_alfa")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every value is the final estimate in the Text S1 control stream, and every
estimated value equals the "Observed value - Median" column of Table 1.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL) | 8.91 L/h | Text S1 `$THETA` 1; Table 1 |
| `lvc` (V_C) | 39 L | Text S1 `$THETA` 2; Table 1 |
| `lq` (Q) | 5.46 L/h | Text S1 `$THETA` 3; Table 1 |
| `lkup` (k_uptake) | 0.00952 1/h, fixed | Text S1 `$THETA` 4 (FIX); Table S1 (Waldmann 1990) |
| `lvendosome` (V_D) | 0.138 L | Text S1 `$THETA` 5; Table 1 |
| `lkrec` (k_recycle) | 0.00107 1/h | Text S1 `$THETA` 6; Table 1 |
| `lkint` (k_int) | 0.375 1/h | Text S1 `$THETA` 7 (estimated, not FIX); Table 1 |
| `lc_il7r_t` (R_tot) | 1360 pmol/L, fixed | Text S1 `$THETA` 8 (FIX); Table S1 (Monti 2013 Figure 3E) |
| `lvabs_im` (V_I, IM) | 442 L | Text S1 `$THETA` 11; Table 1 |
| `lvabs_sc` (V_I, SC) | 1680 L | Text S1 `$THETA` 12; Table 1 |
| `c_fcrn_t` (FcRn) | 91,950,000 pmol/L, fixed | Text S1 `$PK`; Table S1 (Barber 2023) |
| `fr_recycle` (FR) | 0.715, fixed | Text S1 `$PK`; Table S1 (Zhao 2013, Garg 2007) |
| `koff_fcrn`, `kon_fcrn` | 12.132 1/h, 4.068e-4 L/pmol/h | Text S1 `$PK` (`KOFF1`, `KON1`); Methods 2.1 (biolayer interferometry) |
| `koff_il7r`, `kon_il7r` | 59.76 1/h, 2.0196e-3 L/pmol/h | Text S1 `$PK` (`KOFF2`, `KON2`) |
| `etalcl` | 0.347 (64.4 % CV) | Text S1 `$OMEGA` 1; Table 1 |
| `etalq` | 0.659 (96.6 % CV) | Text S1 `$OMEGA` 2; Table 1 |
| `propSd` | 0.335 | Text S1 `$THETA` 9; Table 1 |
| `addSd` | 1.05 pmol/L | Text S1 `$THETA` 10; Table 1 |
| `kss_fcrn`, `kss_il7r` | (k_recycle + k_off1)/k_on1, (k_int + k_off2)/k_on2 | Eqs. (1), (2); Text S1 `$PK` |
| QSS free concentration | quadratic root | Text S1 `$DES`, `$ERROR` |
| `d/dt(abs_site)`, `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(endosome)` | -- | Text S1 `$DES` `DADT(1)`-`DADT(3)`; Figure 1 |
| `f(abs_site) = 2` | -- | Text S1 `$PK` `F1 = 2`, dataset note "AMT: GX-I7 pmol x 2 = IL7 pmol" |
| `ROUTE_SC` switch on V_I | -- | Text S1 `$PK` `VI = VISC; IF(COHORT.EQ.3) VI = VIIM` |
| `Cc ~ prop() + add()` on free conc. | -- | Text S1 `$ERROR`, `$SIGMA 1 FIX` |

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Jeon_2025_efineptakin_alfa")

# ug/kg of rhIL-7-hyFc -> pmol of drug (MW 104 kDa; Methods 2.1)
dose_pmol <- function(ug_per_kg, wt) ug_per_kg * wt * 1e-6 / 104000 * 1e12

# ug/L of IL-7 -> pmol/L (20.5 kDa per IL-7 moiety; Methods 2.1)
ugL_to_pM <- function(x) x * 1e-6 / 20500 * 1e12

# Weight drawn from the trial mean and SD (Lee 2020), as Jeon 2025 describes
# for its own simulations; redraw the rare non-physiological low tail.
draw_wt <- function(n) {
  wt <- rnorm(n, 65.3, 11.1)
  while (any(low <- wt < 40)) wt[low] <- rnorm(sum(low), 65.3, 11.1)
  wt
}

# The study's three cohorts
cohorts <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort,          ~dose_ugkg, ~ROUTE_SC,
  "20 ug/kg s.c.",  20,         1,
  "60 ug/kg i.m.",  60,         0,
  "60 ug/kg s.c.",  60,         1
)
```

# Structural checks (typical subject)

Two identities must hold exactly for any correct implementation, so they are
checked on a typical-value solve at tight tolerances. The cumulative
amount eliminated (linear clearance plus IL-7R-complex internalisation) is
tracked with an extra state appended to the model for this check only.

```{r structural}
ui_mb <- rxode2::rxode2(mod) |>
  rxode2::model(
    {
      d/dt(auc_central) <- Cc
      d/dt(eliminated) <- kel * c_free * vc + kint * c_cpx * vc
    },
    append = TRUE
  )
# An explicit ODE model: rxode2 must not have replaced it by linCmt()
stopifnot(is.null(rxode2::rxode2(mod)$linCmt))

ev_mb <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_pmol(60, 65.3), cmt = "abs_site") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 30000, by = 10)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(ROUTE_SC = 0)
typ_mb <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(ui_mb), ev_mb,
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame"
)
f_in <- 2 * dose_pmol(60, 65.3)

checks <- typ_mb |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  summarise(
    mass_balance_relerr = max(abs(
      (abs_site + central + endosome + eliminated) / f_in - 1
    )),
    qss_central_relerr = max(abs((c_free + c_cpx) / c_tot - 1)),
    qss_endosome_relerr = max(abs((a_free + a_cpx) / a_tot - 1)),
    max_free_over_total = max(c_free / c_tot),
    remaining_at_30000h = last(abs_site + central + endosome) / f_in
  )
tibble(check = names(checks), value = formatC(unlist(checks), format = "g", digits = 3)) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # Every pmol dosed (x2 IL-7 moieties) is in a state or has been eliminated.
  # Measured ~3e-15; a missing or mis-signed flux term moves this by > 1e-3.
  checks$mass_balance_relerr < 1e-8,
  # The rationalised QSS root reproduces the total exactly in both spaces.
  checks$qss_central_relerr < 1e-8,
  checks$qss_endosome_relerr < 1e-8,
  checks$max_free_over_total <= 1
)
```

At microdose and therapeutic concentrations IL-7R binding is far from
saturation (free concentration is almost all of the total; `R_tot` is small
against `K_SS2`), so total exposure follows the linear identity
`AUC(free) x (CL + k_int x V_C x R_tot / K_SS2) = 2 x Dose`:

```{r auc-identity}
p_typ <- typ_mb[1, ]
cl_eff <- p_typ$cl + p_typ$kint * p_typ$vc * p_typ$c_il7r_t / p_typ$kss_il7r
auc_ratio <- last(typ_mb$auc_central) * cl_eff / f_in
auc_ratio
# Measured 0.9999+: the only departure is the tiny non-linearity of the
# IL-7R term, so 1 % separates it from any error in CL, V_C or the dose units.
stopifnot(abs(auc_ratio - 1) < 0.01)
```

The slow phase is the endosomal recycling (`k_recycle` = 0.00107 1/h, a
~650 h half-life), so only about two thirds of this total exposure accrues
within the 672 h sampling window of the trial.

# Virtual cohort and simulation

Each of the three study cohorts is simulated with 200 subjects (the trial
had 8 per cohort) at the trial's sampling times (Lee 2020: 0, 1, 2, 4, 6,
8, 11, 14, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 96, 168, 240, 336, 504 and 672 h) plus a
dense grid for the figure.

```{r cohort}
# rxSetSeed() fixes the draw for a given solver thread count only; every
# assertion below is written to hold for any cohort the model can produce.
set.seed(20250252)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250252)

n_per_arm <- 200
pk_times <- c(0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 11, 14, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 96, 168, 240, 336, 504, 672)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(pk_times, seq(0, 672, by = 4))))

make_cohort <- function(k) {
  row <- cohorts[k, ]
  subj <- tibble(id = (k - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm), WT = draw_wt(n_per_arm))
  dose <- subj |>
    mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "abs_site", amt = dose_pmol(row$dose_ugkg, WT))
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(cohort = row$cohort, ROUTE_SC = row$ROUTE_SC) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohorts)), make_cohort))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("cohort", "WT"),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim$Cc)))
```

# Replicate Figure 2 (VPC)

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 8}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(cohort, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q05), colour = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q95), colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~cohort, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (hour)", y = "Concentration (pM)",
    title = "Simulated 5th / 50th / 95th percentiles of free IL-7",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Jeon 2025 (with residual error)."
  )
```

```{r figure-2-peaks}
sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(cohort, time) |>
  summarise(Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(cohort) |>
  summarise(
    peak_median = max(Q50), time_of_peak_median = time[which.max(Q50)],
    peak_95th = max(Q95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Cohort" = cohort, "Peak median Cc (pmol/L)" = peak_median,
    "Time of peak median (h)" = time_of_peak_median,
    "Peak 95th percentile (pmol/L)" = peak_95th
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Figure 2 is a vector graphic, so the model-predicted confidence interval of
the median (the red band) was digitised by the maintainers from the
article PDF, calibrated on the panel gridlines, at the centre of each VPC
time bin. The simulated median of the observations, pooled over the trial
samples that fall in each bin, is compared with it below.

```{r figure-2-band}
# Digitised from Jeon 2025 Figure 2 (red band = model-predicted CI of the
# median), pmol/L. Bin centres read from the band's vertices; the 60 ug/kg IM
# band at the two latest bins is hidden under the plotted lines.
band <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort,         ~bin_h, ~lower, ~upper,
  "20 ug/kg s.c.",  19,     2.33,   5.76,
  "20 ug/kg s.c.",  54,     1.88,   4.24,
  "20 ug/kg s.c.", 156,     1.08,   2.43,
  "20 ug/kg s.c.", 372,     0.81,   1.59,
  "20 ug/kg s.c.", 669,     0.52,   1.03,
  "60 ug/kg i.m.",  19,    25.94,  57.78,
  "60 ug/kg i.m.",  54,    13.79,  32.62,
  "60 ug/kg i.m.", 156,     4.72,  10.20,
  "60 ug/kg s.c.",  19,     7.86,  18.45,
  "60 ug/kg s.c.",  54,     6.13,  13.69,
  "60 ug/kg s.c.", 156,     3.72,   7.75,
  "60 ug/kg s.c.", 372,     2.21,   4.28,
  "60 ug/kg s.c.", 669,     1.87,   3.55
)
# Trial sampling times pooled into each bin
bin_times <- list(`19` = c(11, 14, 24), `54` = c(48, 60), `156` = 168,
                  `372` = c(336, 504), `669` = 672)
band_cmp <- band |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(sim_median = median(sim$sim[sim$cohort == cohort &
                                       sim$time %in% bin_times[[as.character(bin_h)]]])) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(inside = sim_median >= lower & sim_median <= upper)
band_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Cohort" = cohort, "Bin centre (h)" = bin_h,
    "Band lower (pmol/L)" = lower, "Band upper (pmol/L)" = upper,
    "Simulated median (pmol/L)" = sim_median, "Inside band" = inside
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  nrow(band_cmp) == 13, all(is.finite(band_cmp$sim_median)),
  # All 13 medians sat inside the band across repeated cohorts, the 20 ug/kg
  # late bin within 2 % of its upper edge; a 15 % margin absorbs the cohort
  # draw. The bands span about 2-fold, so a dose-unit error (2x), a wrong route
  # volume or a mis-placed recycling flux falls outside several of them.
  all(band_cmp$sim_median >= band_cmp$lower / 1.15),
  all(band_cmp$sim_median <= band_cmp$upper * 1.15)
)
```

The band itself shows the shape of the published model: after SC dosing
the predicted median is highest in the first bin (about 19 h) and declines
from there, while the observed median (red line in Figure 2) peaks in the
54 h bin. The early plateau and the slow tail at 2-4 pmol/L to 672 h are
both reproduced, and they also explain the NCA comparison below.

# NCA against the trial report

Lee 2020 (Table 1) reports NCA of the baseline-adjusted IL-7 concentrations
by cohort, as mean +/- SD (Tmax as median) in ug/L of IL-7; they are
converted here to pmol/L with the 20.5 kDa per IL-7 used by Jeon 2025.
The trial's NCA was run on measured concentrations, so the comparison uses
simulated **observations** (the `sim` column, which carries the residual
error) at the trial's sampling times, and drops every sample below the
assay's lower limit of quantification (0.031 ng/mL = 1.51 pmol/L), as the
trial could not have measured it. Noise matters here: after SC dosing the
model predicts a broad plateau rather than a sharp peak, and on a plateau
the observed Tmax is decided by assay noise.

```{r pknca}
lloq <- ugL_to_pM(0.031)

nca_conc <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% pk_times) |>
  transmute(id, time, cohort, Cc = if_else(time == 0, 0, sim)) |>
  filter(time == 0 | Cc >= lloq) |>
  arrange(id, time)
stopifnot(all(table(nca_conc$id[nca_conc$time == 0]) == 1))

nca_dose <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, cohort)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | cohort + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | cohort + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

# Lee 2020 reports means (Tmax: median), so summarise the simulation the same way
nca_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(cohort, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(
    PPORRES = if (PPTESTCD[1] == "tmax") median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE) else mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort,         ~cmax,           ~tmax, ~auclast,         ~aucinf.obs,      ~half.life,
  "20 ug/kg s.c.", ugL_to_pM(0.1),  42.0,  ugL_to_pM(10.2),  ugL_to_pM(12.4),  52.7,
  "60 ug/kg s.c.", ugL_to_pM(0.5),  36.0,  ugL_to_pM(31.0),  ugL_to_pM(33.3),  26.8,
  "60 ug/kg i.m.", ugL_to_pM(1.2),  4.0,   ugL_to_pM(64.9),  ugL_to_pM(83.4),  63.3
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_sim,
  reference = published,
  by = "cohort",
  units = c(cmax = "pmol/L", tmax = "h", auclast = "pmol*h/L",
            aucinf.obs = "pmol*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated (200/cohort) vs. Lee 2020 Table 1 NCA (8/cohort). * differs by >20%."
)
```

```{r nca-gate}
cmax_ratio <- nca_sim |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  left_join(published |> select(cohort, cmax), by = "cohort") |>
  mutate(ratio = PPORRES / cmax)
cmax_ratio
stopifnot(
  nrow(cmax_ratio) == 3,
  # The peak scale pins the dose units (pmol of drug x 2 IL-7). Doubling or
  # halving the IL-7 count moves every ratio by 2x; the observed means come
  # from 8 subjects per cohort and Lee 2020 rounds Cmax to 0.1 ug/L, so the
  # gate is on the median ratio across the three cohorts.
  median(cmax_ratio$ratio) > 0.6,
  median(cmax_ratio$ratio) < 1.6
)
```

Cmax is close to the trial for the two 60 ug/kg cohorts and higher for 20
ug/kg SC, where the additive residual error (1.05 pmol/L) is a fifth of the
peak and Lee 2020 rounds the mean Cmax to 0.1 ug/L (4.9 pmol/L). The other
rows differ for reasons that belong to the published model, not to this
implementation, since the same model reproduces the authors' own VPC band
above:

* **Tmax after SC** is about 11 h in simulation against 36-42 h in the trial.
  The model predicts an early plateau (the input `Q / V_I` from the injection
  site is fastest at the start), which is the shape of the paper's own
  predicted-median band.
* **AUC and half-life.** FcRn recycling returns drug to serum at
  `k_recycle` = 0.00107 1/h, so the model keeps 2-4 pmol/L in serum to 672 h
  (the late bins of the band). The simulated AUClast therefore runs
  1.7-2.4 times the trial's, and the terminal half-life fitted to that tail
  is hundreds of hours against the trial's 27-63 h. The trial's NCA did not
  capture a tail of this size, and AUC to infinity, which extrapolates it,
  differs most.

# Replicate Figure 3 (dose selection)

Jeon 2025 simulated IM regimens and called a regimen safe for a subject if
its AUC was no larger than the median AUC of the maximum tolerated regimen,
1200 ug/kg Q3W (the MTD of trial NCT03478995), and effective if the trough
(baseline plus exogenous IL-7) reached the EC50 of 18.1907 pmol/L from a
lymphocyte proliferation assay. The probability of each criterion across
1000 subjects was plotted against dose (Figure 3), and doses where both
exceeded 0.8 were proposed: 670-800 ug/kg Q3W, 1010-1530 ug/kg Q6W and
1510-2190 ug/kg Q9W. Q1W met efficacy at every dose and safety at none.

The paper does not state the AUC window. Its Discussion treats 2400 ug/kg
Q6W and 3600 ug/kg Q9W as exposure-equivalent to 1200 ug/kg Q3W, so AUC is
compared here over a common 18-week window (the least common multiple of 3,
6 and 9 weeks) of repeated dosing. The trough is the concentration at the
end of the first dosing interval, the lowest of the regimen since exposure
only accumulates afterwards.

```{r figure-3-sim}
ui_auc <- rxode2::rxode2(mod) |>
  rxode2::model(d/dt(auc_central) <- Cc, append = TRUE)

horizon <- 18 * 168
dose_grid <- list(
  "Q1W" = c(300, 600, 900, 1200),
  "Q3W" = c(300, 600, 800, 1200, 1800, 2400, 3600),
  "Q6W" = c(300, 1000, 1530, 2400, 3600, 5400, 7200),
  "Q9W" = c(300, 1500, 2190, 3600, 5400, 7200, 10800)
)
arms <- bind_rows(lapply(names(dose_grid), function(r) {
  tibble(regimen = r, tau_wk = as.numeric(sub("Q(\\d+)W", "\\1", r)), dose_ugkg = dose_grid[[r]])
})) |>
  mutate(arm = row_number())

n_fig3 <- 200
make_regimen <- function(k) {
  a <- arms[k, ]
  tau <- a$tau_wk * 168
  subj <- tibble(id = (k - 1L) * n_fig3 + seq_len(n_fig3), WT = draw_wt(n_fig3))
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(subj, time = seq(0, horizon - tau, by = tau)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "abs_site", amt = dose_pmol(a$dose_ugkg, WT))
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(subj, time = c(tau, horizon)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(arm = a$arm, ROUTE_SC = 0) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
ev3 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), make_regimen))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev3[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_auc, events = ev3, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(arms, by = "arm")
stopifnot(all(is.finite(sim3$auc_central)))

auc_ref <- sim3 |>
  filter(regimen == "Q3W", dose_ugkg == 1200, time == horizon) |>
  pull(auc_central) |>
  median()
ec50 <- 18.1907

prob <- bind_rows(
  sim3 |>
    filter(time == horizon) |>
    group_by(regimen, dose_ugkg) |>
    summarise(p = mean(auc_central <= auc_ref), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(criterion = "Safety (AUC <= AUC at 1200 ug/kg Q3W)"),
  sim3 |>
    filter(time == tau_wk * 168) |>
    group_by(regimen, dose_ugkg) |>
    summarise(p = mean(Cc >= ec50), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(criterion = "Efficacy, exogenous IL-7 only (trough >= EC50)")
)
```

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(prob, aes(dose_ugkg, p, colour = criterion)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("red", "blue")) +
  labs(
    x = "Dose (ug/kg IM)", y = "Probability", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Jeon 2025 (200 subjects per dose)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The dose at which each probability crosses 0.8 is read off by linear
interpolation and compared with the published bounds:

```{r figure-3-bounds}
# First change of (p >= 0.8) along the dose grid: rising for efficacy,
# falling for safety.
cross80 <- function(dose, p) {
  i <- which(diff(p >= 0.8) != 0)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) stop("probability does not cross 0.8 within the dose grid")
  dose[i] + (0.8 - p[i]) * (dose[i + 1] - dose[i]) / (p[i + 1] - p[i])
}
crossings <- prob |>
  filter(regimen != "Q1W") |>
  arrange(regimen, criterion, dose_ugkg) |>
  group_by(regimen, criterion) |>
  summarise(dose_at_0.8 = cross80(dose_ugkg, p), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(published = case_when(
    regimen == "Q3W" & grepl("^Safety", criterion) ~ 800,
    regimen == "Q6W" & grepl("^Safety", criterion) ~ 1530,
    regimen == "Q9W" & grepl("^Safety", criterion) ~ 2190,
    regimen == "Q3W" ~ 670,
    regimen == "Q6W" ~ 1010,
    regimen == "Q9W" ~ 1510
  ))
crossings |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Criterion" = criterion,
    "Simulated dose at P = 0.8 (ug/kg)" = dose_at_0.8,
    "Published bound (ug/kg)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0)

safety <- crossings |> filter(grepl("^Safety", criterion))
efficacy <- crossings |> filter(grepl("^Efficacy", criterion))
q1w_safe <- prob |> filter(regimen == "Q1W", grepl("^Safety", criterion))
stopifnot(
  nrow(safety) == 3, nrow(efficacy) == 3,
  # Safety bounds: the 0.8 crossing of a 200-subject proportion moves by about
  # +/-5 % between draws (measured 742-792 / 1496-1552 / 2122-2259 ug/kg across
  # repeated cohorts); 15 % is > 3 Monte-Carlo SE and still fails if the IIV
  # on CL or Q, or the slow recycling tail, is mis-transcribed.
  all(abs(safety$dose_at_0.8 / safety$published - 1) < 0.15),
  # Efficacy: endogenous IL-7 can only add to the trough, so the exogenous-only
  # dose must be at least the published lower bound (10 % Monte-Carlo margin).
  all(efficacy$dose_at_0.8 > 0.9 * efficacy$published),
  # Q1W: the published curve is never safe. At 300 ug/kg the expected
  # proportion is ~0.70, too close to 0.8 for a 200-subject draw, so the gate
  # covers 600 ug/kg and above (expected <= 0.2).
  all(q1w_safe$p[q1w_safe$dose_ugkg >= 600] < 0.8)
)
```

The safety bounds are reproduced. The efficacy curve here omits each
subject's baseline IL-7, because Jeon 2025 sampled baselines from the
observed mean and SD without reporting them; the exogenous-only crossings
therefore sit above the published lower bounds (670, 1010 and 1510 ug/kg),
by the margin that baseline IL-7 contributes to the trough.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose units.** The control stream doses pmol of rhIL-7-hyFc into the
  injection site with `F1 = 2`, annotated "AMT: GX-I7 pmol x 2 = IL7 pmol".
  The maintainers read this as AMT = pmol of drug and `F1 = 2` performing the
  doubling (dose in `units$dosing`). Figure 2 and the Lee 2020 Cmax values
  confirm it; doubling a second time would place the 20 ug/kg SC median
  near the observed 95th percentile.
* **QSS root.** The control stream computes the free concentration as
  `0.5 * (D + sqrt(D^2 + 4 * KSS * Ctot))`. The model uses the algebraically
  identical rationalised root `2 * KSS * Ctot / (sqrt(D^2 + 4 * KSS * Ctot) - D)`.
  In the endosome `D` is about -9.2e7 pmol/L (FcRn is 92 uM), and the
  printed form loses precision to cancellation at low drug amounts; the
  structural check above confirms both roots reproduce the total.
* **`K_SS1`.** The control stream writes `KSS1 = KD + Krec/KON1` with
  `KD = 29823` hard-coded; the model computes `(k_recycle + k_off1)/k_on1`
  (Eq. 1), whose `k_off1/k_on1 = 29823.009` differs from 29823 by 3e-7 relative.
* **IV dosing.** `F2 = 2` in the control stream is kept as `f(central) = 2`
  for completeness; the trial had no IV arm.
* **Demographics** for the virtual cohorts (weight 65.3 +/- 11.1 kg) come
  from the primary trial report (Lee 2020), since Jeon 2025 does not tabulate
  them. Weight affects only the ug/kg dose.
* **Figure 3 interpretation.** The AUC window for the safety criterion and
  the definition of the trough are not stated in the paper; the choices
  above (18-week common window of repeated dosing; trough at the end of the
  first interval) are the maintainers' and reproduce the published safety
  bounds. Simulations use 200 subjects per dose instead of 1000.
* **Baseline IL-7** for the efficacy criterion is not reported, so the
  efficacy curve is exogenous-only and its lower bounds are checked one-sided.
* **Covariates.** None retained; age, sex, weight, height and BMI are
  listed in `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* No erratum to Jeon 2025 was found (checked 2026-10-15).
